notes.inflation: Inflation is the EU's harmonised index (HICP), the measure the ECB targets. Statistics Finland's national CPI usually differs by a few tenths, because it includes owner-occupied housing and interest on consumer loans, which HICP leaves out. Finland has no policy rate of its own: the rate shown is the European Central Bank's deposit facility rate, set for the whole euro area.
notes.labour: Unemployment is Eurostat's monthly, seasonally adjusted rate (ILO definition, ages 15 to 74). Finnish news usually quotes Statistics Finland's unadjusted monthly figure, or its trend, so headlines can differ by several tenths. Employment and participation rates are the OECD's quarterly figures for ages 15 to 64.
notes.trade: Goods trade is Eurostat's monthly total with the rest of the world, in euros. Finland's goods trade is close to balance; single deliveries of ships or aircraft can swing a month by several hundred million euros.
notes.public: Debt and the budget balance are Eurostat's excessive deficit procedure figures for general government, calendar years, so the latest year is a year ahead of the IMF's.
notes.markets: The 10-year yield is the OECD's monthly average of the Finnish government yield, shown from March 1990 because the source has no value for February 1990; the exchange rates are the Federal Reserve's daily euro rates, shared with every euro area page.
